mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls >5% month-on-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.3% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE > 4.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months, combined with a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1%, signals supply-side stress that elevates input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98 for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes of three consecutive months with INDPRO < 98 and RSAFS falling >1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 320 for two consecutive months, coinciding with a federal funds rate above 4.0%, signals a risk of disinflation or deflation, which historically has been associated with equity market weakness over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 320 for 2 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 4.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive months with CPIAUCSL < 320 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 coincident with an unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes higher wage inflation and margin compression, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of monthly PAYEMS > 100,000 and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive quarters with GDPC1 annualized < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1.5% for two consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive months with INDPRO monthly change > 1.5%.
